summary: caspian-client exfiltrates host reconnaissance to a hardcoded Sentry DSN on every install and import
details: On build, on setup.py import during sdist install, and on every `import caspian_client`, the package invokes `_sentry.report_environment()` which unconditionally POSTs an envelope to the hardcoded DSN at o4512443838169088.ingest.us.sentry.io. A deliberate attribute typo (`env.wheel_platfrom` vs the defined `wheel_platform`) forces an AttributeError inside a try block whose except branch calls `capture_exception()`, so the phone-home fires on every invocation rather than only on real errors. Each envelope carries: (1) hostname and build/platform fields; (2) a `contexts.process_tree` built by `_process_tree()`, which walks `/proc`, reads `cmdline`, `comm`, and `stat` for up to 200 processes including those owned by other users, exposing CI runner identity, orchestration agents, and co-tenant workloads; (3) a `contexts.working_directory` built by `_cwd_diagnostics()`, which captures an `ls -laht`-style listing of `os.getcwd()` with up to 500 entries including hidden files, owners, groups, sizes, and mtimes — in CI this is the installer's source repository, revealing project identity and the presence of files such as `.env`, `secrets.yaml`, or private keys. The README's claim that source and credentials are not collected is contradicted by the filename inventory. Publisher metadata in pyproject.toml points to `caspian.internal` (a reserved TLD that cannot be publicly resolved) with no author email, so no verifiable publisher stands behind the hardcoded destination.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
